coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Arden
record.summary: Arden is a 16-story condominium development at 708-718 Long Bridge Street along Mission Creek, developed by Bosa Development; the Assessor lists 267 unit parcels there with 2016 as the year built, while DBI's new-construction permit (263 dwelling units, 16 stories, filed December 2012) was not recorded complete until February 2019.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint(s), not a hand trace or plan estimate. The underlying Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across many individually owned per-unit lots (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data), so no single blklot represents the whole building and the building cannot be mapped from a single Assessor parcel the way a single-owner building can. Using the real building footprint from OSM instead of a fabricated or arbitrarily chosen 'representative' unit lot, the same real-geometry-without-a-single-parcel pattern already used for several Pier 70 buildings (DataSF Building Footprints) and for Mission Bay's own real park polygons.

changes.text: Added a sourced dossier for Arden.

Arden's completion milestone said June 2016; its cited source, Kinoko Real Estate's Arden page, says only 'Completed in 2016', so it now reads 2016 and cites that page instead of a bare domain. A 2014 milestone saying Arden was under construction, sold out and targeting fall 2015 was removed: it cited only the bare domain livabl.com, no page could be found or read, and nothing else read confirms it. The map notes also flag that the 267-unit figure is not stated by either cited source.

open_questions: No primary opening or first-occupancy date found: the Assessor's 2016 is a year only, and the DBI permit's 2019-02-08 completion is a permit sign-off. The sales-agent page, SF Highrises and the Assessor say 2016; the architecture database says 2014 (and 2013-2014 for construction).
Unit count differs: 263 (DBI, architecture database) versus 267 (SF Highrises; 267 Assessor unit parcels counted).
Architect rests on a sales-agent page and the architecture database (both secondary); no OCII, Planning or architect source read.
Groundbreaking date not found (the DBI permit's first construction document date, 2013-12-06, is not a groundbreaking).
A Business Times article cited by the architecture database ('Bosa prepares next Mission Bay site', March 2013) could not be opened (blocked); not relied on.
No OCII design-review or commission item for Block 12 East was located.
